_meta.purpose: Whole-page templates the picker chooses from a 4.0 brief (engine.page_sequence.select_for_brief): an explicit page_sequence first, then stage, then the industry, product_type and project_type fields and the brief's phrases. A single call-to-action verb never keys a sequence. A section with a proof kind renders only with the client's real proof of that kind; the picker drops it with a stated reason when the brief's proof list lacks it. mechanism_needs names what each conversion mechanism needs (a proof kind or a contact route).

section_sequence.purpose: Capture the lead at first paint. Text left (headline + one-line value + phone affordance), inline quote or contact form right. The form is the wow moment and the conversion path -- never buried below.
A thin band of 3-5 real, organic numbers (jobs completed, years operating, response time, coverage radius) directly under the hero -- instant credibility before the scroll.
3-5 cards naming the concrete reasons to choose this service (speed, price transparency, licensing, same-day). Each card has a tight heading and one sentence.
Every service category / sector the business covers, rendered as a scannable row of pills. Map EVERY sector from the source into a pill -- do not trim to a tidy few.
Every concrete offering (every skip size, every package, every product line) as its own card with a spec line and an action. Completeness over neatness: one source item -> one card.
2-column zig-zag rows that expand the marquee differentiators with depth -- alternating media/text, each row earning its own visual. Not a 3-equal-card grid.
Where the service operates -- a map, a region list, or a coverage statement. For a local/commercial service this answers the 'do you cover me?' question that gates the lead.
A named, quantified testimonial or a strong pull-quote with attribution (name, role/company). One strong quote beats fifteen vibes-only blurbs.
A focused conversion band repeating the primary action (get a quote / call now) with the phone affordance, after the page has earned the click.
A sitemap footer: services, coverage areas, company, contact (phone + hours), legal. Generosity after the page's restraint -- never a thin one-row strip.

entries.cta_placement: Primary lead-capture in the hero (inline form) and repeated in a dedicated CTA band before the footer; phone number persistent in header and CTA band.
entries.footer: Rich sitemap footer: Services, Coverage areas, Company, Contact (phone + hours), Legal.
entries.notes: The inline hero form is the conversion path. Proof and the phone come from the client: a proof section renders only with the client's real numbers or named quotes, and the phone affordance only with a real number; without them the picker drops them and says why. Map every sector into a pill, every size or package into an item card, every benefit into a value card. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.

section_sequence.purpose: Asymmetric hero: value headline + one-line lede + primary CTA on one side, a real product mock (screenshot or interactive demo) on the other. The mock is the proof.
A single monochrome customer-logo row near the hero -- social proof before the feature tour. Skip if there are no real logos.
3-5 outcome-led cards (not feature lists), each with a concrete claim with a number where possible.
3-5 marquee feature sections, each a 2-column zig-zag with a deep visual (annotated screenshot, before/after, synthetic UI). Depth over a dense feature grid.
The integrations or ecosystem the product plugs into, as a labelled grid of marks. Maps EVERY integration the source lists.
A stats band of real outcomes (latency, time saved, adoption) -- organic numbers, not round marketing figures.
A named, quantified customer quote or mini case study with attribution and a real metric.
A 'starts at $X' teaser linking out to full pricing -- never a full pricing table on the homepage.
A focused sign-up / start-free band repeating the single primary action.
Sitemap footer by audience: Product, Solutions, Resources, Company, Legal.

entries.cta_placement: Single primary CTA (start free / sign up) in the hero, repeated in the CTA band; secondary 'see the demo' allowed once in the hero.
entries.footer: Sitemap footer by audience: Product, Solutions, Resources, Company, Legal.
entries.notes: One primary path. Map every integration into the integrations grid and every differentiator into its own split feature row. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.

section_sequence.purpose: Product imagery gallery on one side, buy box (title, price, variant pickers, add-to-cart) on the other. The buy box is the conversion path, above the fold.
A thin band of trust signals: free shipping threshold, returns window, secure checkout, in-stock status.
Cards covering the concrete reasons to buy (materials, warranty, what's in the box) and a spec line.
Every variant, size, or option as a selectable card/swatch. Map EVERY option the source lists -- one variant, one tile.
Zig-zag rows telling the product story with real photography or detail shots -- craft, use, results.
Real, attributed reviews with a rating distribution -- named, specific, not 'amazing!'.
A small, curated set of related products -- not an endless grid.
The objection-handling section: shipping, returns, sizing, care. Answers the questions that block checkout.
A sticky or repeated add-to-cart band so the conversion action is always reachable.
Sitemap footer: Shop, Help (shipping/returns), Company, Legal, contact.

entries.cta_placement: Add-to-cart in the buy box above the fold, made persistent via a sticky bar and repeated in a CTA band.
entries.footer: Sitemap footer: Shop, Help (shipping & returns), Company, Legal, contact.
entries.notes: Conversion is the buy box. Vary image aspect ratios; never clip every shot to 1:1. Map every variant into the option grid; every spec into a card. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.

section_sequence.purpose: A confident positioning statement with a peek of selected work. Editorial, asymmetric -- the work carries the page.
An irregular, editorial grid of case studies (varied aspect ratios, generous gaps). Each tile is a real project, not a card box.
What the studio does, as capability cards or a list. Map EVERY discipline the source lists.
1-3 deep case studies as zig-zag rows: problem, approach, result with a real metric.
How the studio works -- a few honest steps, not numbered chapter signposting for its own sake.
A monochrome client-logo wall or named testimonials with attribution.
Who's behind the work -- real people, real photos or styled portraits.
A direct 'start a project / let's talk' band with a real contact path.
Sitemap footer: Work, Services, About, Contact, social.

entries.cta_placement: Primary 'start a project / get in touch' in the hero secondary slot and repeated in a dedicated CTA band; contact details in the footer.
entries.footer: Sitemap footer: Work, Services, About, Contact, social.
entries.notes: The work is the proof; description is supplementary. Use varied image ratios and an irregular grid -- never a tidy 3-equal-card row. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.

section_sequence.purpose: A masthead with the lead story given editorial weight -- big headline, real image, byline. Sets the publication's voice.
An editorial grid of featured pieces with varied prominence (one dominant, several secondary) -- not equal cards.
Every section/topic the publication covers, as a row of pills. Map EVERY category from the source.
A scannable list of recent pieces with byline, date, and reading time -- typographic, not boxed.
A highlighted piece or a pull-quote that carries the editorial point of view, with attribution.
An inline newsletter capture (not a timed modal) with a clear value line and a single email field.
Who writes here -- real contributors with names and roles.
A focused subscribe band repeating the newsletter or membership action.
Sitemap footer: Sections, Archive, About, Subscribe, legal.

entries.cta_placement: Inline newsletter / subscribe capture mid-page and repeated in a CTA band; never a first-paint modal.
entries.footer: Sitemap footer: Sections, Archive, About, Subscribe, legal.
entries.notes: Typography and hierarchy carry the page. Map every topic into a category pill and every recent piece into the list. Newsletter capture is inline, never a timed interstitial. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.

section_sequence.purpose: A device mock (real app screen) beside a value headline and app-store badges. The store badges are the conversion path, above the fold.
A thin band of real numbers (downloads, rating, active users) -- organic, not round marketing figures.
3-5 cards naming what the app does for the user, each with a concrete benefit.
Real app screenshots in device frames showing the key flows -- varied, not all clipped to one ratio.
Zig-zag rows expanding the marquee features with a screenshot each -- depth over a dense grid.
Named, specific app-store reviews or a rating breakdown -- not 'great app!'.
A short, honest set of steps from install to value.
A focused download band repeating the store badges and the single primary action.
Sitemap footer: App, Support, Company, Legal, store links.

entries.cta_placement: App-store badges in the hero and repeated in a download CTA band; rating shown near the badges as a trust signal.
entries.footer: Sitemap footer: App, Support, Company, Legal, store links.
entries.notes: Conversion is the store badge. Use real device-framed screenshots with varied crops. Map every feature into a split row and every screen into the gallery. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.

section_sequence.purpose: Who buys from whom, in one headline, and the primary action: open an account or request access. A real product view (the catalog, an order, the app) on the other side. The supplier path is a secondary link, never a second filled button.
Two panels side by side, one per side of the market, each with what that side gets and its own action. Unequal widths when one side is the main audience.
Every category the catalog carries, as a scannable list or pills. Counts only when the client gives real ones.
Three to five steps from search to delivery: search, compare, order, receive, pay. Real screens where the client has them.
The marquee capabilities (reorder, price comparison, credit, tracking), each a row with a real screen.
Where it delivers, how fast, and the payment terms (credit, cash on delivery, invoices). This answers the questions a trade buyer asks before an account.
Real numbers from the client (buyers, suppliers, orders, cities). Only numbers the client has measured.
One named quote from a real buyer or supplier, with the business name and city.

section_sequence.section: CTA band (open an account, or join as a supplier)
section_sequence.purpose: The primary action repeated, with the supplier path as a secondary link.
The objections that stop a trade account: minimum order, delivery windows, returns, credit, who can register.
Sitemap footer: For buyers, For suppliers, Categories, Company, Contact, Legal, app store links when there is an app.

entries.cta_placement: Open an account (or request access) in the hero and the CTA band; the supplier path as a secondary link in both; the app store links in the footer when there is an app.
entries.footer: Rich sitemap footer: For buyers, For suppliers, Categories, Company, Contact, Legal.
entries.notes: A marketplace sells to two sides at once; the page names both and leads with the side the brief names as the main audience. Show the real catalog and ordering screens. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.

section_sequence.purpose: What the product will do and for whom, in one headline. The early-access form is the call to action. The launch status is stated plainly: a date, a season, or in private pilot.
The problem the product solves, in the audience's own words. No figure the client has not measured.
Three to five honest steps, or a real prototype screen labelled as a prototype.
What joining now gives: first access, founding pricing, a say in what gets built. Only what the client will honor.
The real team or founder, named, and why they are building it. Before there are customers, the people are the reason to believe.
When it launches, what it will cost, where it works, what happens to the email address.
The early-access form repeated, with the launch status.
Contact, legal, social. Short, since there is little to map yet.

entries.cta_placement: The early-access form in the hero and repeated in the CTA band; nothing else asks for the visitor's details.
entries.notes: No proof section before there is proof. A page that shows invented numbers, quotes or client marks spends the trust it is asking for. When a pilot gives real results, move to the live sequence for the business. Icons follow the one icon rule in commands/ux-design.md: one set per page, an icon only where it says something distinct about its item.
